idea: Implement the Erdős–Soifer family directly: for each k, start from the k×k grid of cells of side 1/k and replace one m×m block of cells by an (m+1)×(m+1) grid of squares of side m/((m+1)k). This adds 2m+1 squares and m/k to the total, so n = k²+2m+1 gives k + m/k. Evaluate every feasible (k, m) for the given n, pad any surplus with size-zero squares, and keep the best.
